The page gives no area; the 40 km radius around Opava stands for the duchy.

correction.text: Opava with the Duchy of Racibórz

keyframe_review.note: 1336/1337: Nicholas II is vested with the Duchy of Racibórz when Leszek dies without heirs ('When Leszek died without heirs in 1336'; 'From 1337 onwards, the Přemyslid dukes also ruled the adjacent former Piast Duchy of Racibórz'); ruled both until his death in 1365.
'In 1377, Duke John I again separated Opava from the duchies of Racibórz and Krnov.'

ledger.note: 1269: Ottokar II of Bohemia carves the lordship of Opava out of the Margraviate of Moravia for his natural son Nicholas I, 'split off from the Margraviate of Moravia before 1269'; Nicholas first appears as 'Lord of Opava' in 1269. The page says 'before 1269'.

1318: 'Opava was officially raised to a duchy in 1318', confirmed as a fief for Nicholas II (Bohemian vassal since 1327 for Racibórz; the lordship had been pawned to Bolesław III in 1310-1311 and 'redeemed by King John of Bohemia in 1311').

1336: Racibórz joins Opava. 'When Leszek died without heirs in 1336' John of Bohemia vested Nicholas II with the Duchy of Racibórz, held 'in personal union' (the body also says 'From 1337 onwards'): the pages differ by a year.
1377: 'Duke John I again separated Opava from the duchies of Racibórz and Krnov'; Opava was granted to his younger brothers.

1485: 'Victor in turn had to cede it to the Bohemian anti-king Matthias Corvinus in 1485' (George of Poděbrady had given it to his son Victor in 1465); Matthias installed his illegitimate son John as duke.

1506: 'King Vladislas II Jagiellon of Bohemia granted Opava to Duke Casimir II of Cieszyn', held to 1528; in 1521 'the Opava line of the Přemyslids had finally become extinct' and the duchy fell back to the Bohemian Crown, from 1526 Habsburg.
1614: Prince Karl I of Liechtenstein 'was invested with the Duchy of Troppau in 1614' by Emperor Matthias; in 1620 he acquired the Duchy of Krnov.

ledger.note: 1742: 'In 1742, in the course of the First Silesian War and the Treaty of Breslau, the Duchy was divided once more.' The northern part, including Głubczyce and Hlučín, went to Prussia.

notes:
The Duchy of Opava is a state Cliopatria lacks (an additional Silesian-Moravian duchy of the region and era with a Wikipedia article and more than ten years of life). One page only (budget 1-2). Bohemian suzerainty (fief of the Bohemian Crown; Leszek of Racibórz a Bohemian vassal since 1327) is the overlord's ledger: kingdom-of-bohemia should carry the vassal events for duchy-of-opava.

Not settled: (1) 1336 (Leszek's death, page) against 1337 (the Přemyslids rule Racibórz, page). (2) The 40 km radius is a stand-in; the page gives no area. (3) The Duchy of Krnov (Jägerndorf) and the Piast Racibórz after 1377 are outside this dossier; krnov needs one. (4) The end is the 1742 division; the Austrian Duchy of Troppau continued to 1918 inside Austrian Silesia (habsburg-monarchy). (5) The rename events are changes of dynasty within the duchy.
